sections.h2: The law that governs Alabama rentals
sections.html:
Residential rentals in Alabama fall under the Uniform Residential Landlord and Tenant Act, Title 35, Chapter 9A of the Code of Alabama, passed as Act 2006-316. It is arranged in six articles: general provisions, landlord obligations, tenant obligations, remedies, retaliatory conduct, and the effective date and savings provisions.

Squatting lives in a separate chapter, Chapter 9B, outside the landlord and tenant act. If someone occupies a property with no lease and no permission, start there instead of with the rental rules.

sections.h2: Disclosure duty and who inherits it
sections.html:
Section 35-9A-202 requires a landlord, or anyone authorized to sign a lease for the landlord, to tell the tenant in writing, at or before the start of the tenancy, who manages the property and who the owner or the owner's agent is for service of process and notices.

If you plan to sell, two points matter. The information has to stay current, and the section binds any successor landlord, owner or manager. So whoever buys a rental takes on the disclosure duty, and a seller who is leaving should pass along a clean record of what the tenant was told. Keep a dated copy of the written disclosure in your sale file.

Silence carries a penalty. A person who fails to comply becomes an agent of each landlord for receiving notices and demands and for performing the landlord's obligations under the chapter and the rental agreement. That can drag a former or distant owner into disputes they thought they had left.

Maintenance duties come from Section 35-9A-204. A landlord must follow building and housing codes that materially affect health and safety, make the repairs that keep the unit habitable, and keep common areas clean and safe.

  • Keep electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating and air-conditioning systems, and any supplied appliances, in good and safe working order.
  • Provide garbage receptacles and arrange removal.
  • Supply running water, a reasonable amount of hot water and reasonable heat, unless the building is not required to have heat or the tenant controls the system through a direct public utility connection.

If a code duty is greater than any other duty on the list, the code duty controls. A tenant loses these rights when the tenant, a family member or a guest caused the condition through a willful or negligent act.

sections.h2: Can a tenant agree to do repairs?
sections.html:
Sometimes. For a single-family home, landlord and tenant may agree in writing that the tenant takes over the garbage and water duties along with specified repairs, maintenance, alterations and remodeling.

Other dwellings face stricter terms. The deal must be a separate signed writing supported by adequate consideration, the work cannot be needed to cure a code violation, and it cannot reduce the landlord's duties to other tenants. The landlord also cannot make the side agreement a condition of the lease itself.

If you are selling a house whose tenant handles upkeep, expect the buyer to ask for that writing, since the statute calls for one.

sections.h2: Ending a lease for unpaid rent or a violation
sections.html:
Under Section 35-9A-421, the landlord sends a written notice ending the lease. The termination date must fall at least seven business days after the tenant receives it, and the tenant has until then to fix the problem.

Ground for ending the leaseWhat the statute requires
Material noncompliance with the leaseWritten notice that specifies the acts or omissions, with an end date at least seven business days after receipt, unless the tenant remedies the breach first
Unpaid rentWritten notice stating rent and late fees owed, with termination not less than seven business days after receipt if unpaid
Intentional misrepresentation of a material fact in the lease or applicationCannot be remedied or cured
Both grounds at onceThe unpaid rent period governs

A landlord may also seek actual damages and reasonable attorney fees, and an injunction, for a tenant's noncompliance.

The same section restricts cures. A tenant may not cure a breach of the lease more than two times in any 12-month period without the landlord's written consent.

Some acts count as noncurable defaults. The landlord may end the lease on seven days' notice, with no right to remedy unless the landlord agrees:

  • Drug activity of any sort inside the unit or the shared areas.
  • Unlawful use or discharge of a gun or ammunition on the premises, other than self-defense and cases the statute lists.
  • A criminal assault on a tenant or a guest at the property, with the same self-defense and listed exceptions.
  • Repeating, within six months, substantially the same conduct that was already noticed and cured.

sections.h2: Selling a rental house with a tenant
sections.html:
A tenant-occupied sale means extra paperwork, and the statutes above set the baseline. A buyer's attorney or title company will usually review the lease, the disclosure information, the repair history and any pending notices before closing.

Gather these before you list or take an offer:

  • The signed lease and any written maintenance agreement with the tenant.
  • The written disclosure of the manager and the owner or agent that the tenant received.
  • Copies of any termination notice, with the date the tenant received it, since the seven business day count starts at receipt.
  • A record of repairs made under the landlord's duties and any code notices.

A sitting tenant does not always get in the way. Certain buyers want occupied rentals, while some owners prefer to sell vacant. Either way, the buyer's lender or attorney may ask how long the lease runs and whether the rent is current. If the lease is month-to-month or the tenant has stopped paying, how and when you end the tenancy shapes the timeline, so ask an Alabama attorney which notice fits your facts.

sections.h2: Cash sale of an occupied house
sections.html:
It is possible. A cash buyer does not wait on mortgage underwriting or an appraisal, and an investor who buys rentals can take a house in the condition it is in.

That covers houses with deferred repairs under the landlord's duties, late-paying tenants and mixed paperwork. You still need to be straight about the lease, the tenant's status and any notice that has been served. If you would rather close and move on, ask for an offer on the house as it stands and decide afterward. You owe nothing if you say no.

faqs.q: How much notice does an Alabama landlord give for unpaid rent?
faqs.a: A written notice stating the rent and late fees owed, with termination not less than seven business days after the tenant receives it. Paying inside that window keeps the lease alive.

faqs.q: Can a tenant fix a lease violation after getting a notice?
faqs.a: Usually, within the notice period. Cures are capped at two per 12 months without the landlord's written consent, and some acts, such as drug use, certain firearm violations and criminal assault, cannot be cured.

faqs.q: What repairs must an Alabama landlord make?
faqs.a: Follow health and safety codes, keep the unit habitable, maintain electrical, plumbing, heating and cooling systems and supplied appliances, handle garbage removal, and supply running water, reasonable hot water and reasonable heat, with limited exceptions.

faqs.q: Does a buyer of a rental take over the landlord's disclosure duty?
faqs.a: Yes. The duty extends to and can be enforced against any successor landlord, owner or manager, and the information has to stay current.

faqs.q: Can a tenant agree to maintain the house?
faqs.a: For a single-family home, yes, through a written agreement covering garbage, water and specified repairs. For other dwellings it takes a separate signed writing, and it cannot cover work needed to cure a code violation.
